title: Mixed Signals: Weight-Space Programming for EEG and ECG
tasks_benchmarks: PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery (eyes open/closed, left/right fist, fists/feet)

headline_result.text: Writing all 2,730 weights of an EEG classifier from zero using 5 practice subjects, Claude Opus 5.5 reached 0.834 balanced accuracy on 65 unseen subjects, versus 0.704 for gradient descent on 5 subjects and 0.806 on 30; no model improved an already healthy network.
headline_result.quote: A TinyEEGNet network, with all its weights initialized to 0, is written through the reasoning of Claude Opus 5.5 using only 5 training subjects, and matches the same network trained by gradient descent on 30 training subjects.

notes_for_review: One of the better-controlled WSP studies: success rules fixed in advance, random-edit placebo, untrained/shuffled-label control networks, fine-tuning and last-layer retraining baselines, and three editor LLMs (two open-weight). The from-scratch EEG result rests on one run per model and a public dataset the editor recognized, and the comparison is against gradient descent on a 2,730-weight network trained with very few subjects. Negative findings (cannot read task from weights, cannot improve healthy nets, invisible faults fixed by feedback-driven trial rather than diagnosis) are reported clearly. The text is two-column and quotes here are taken from single extracted lines.
